# Cornelia Bryant

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v4 c6 P40](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0040)</sub>
- **Role:** old maid  <sub>[v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019), [v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005)</sub>

## Appearance

Miss Cornelia has a fresh, round, pink-and-white face with jolly, kindly brown eyes. She wears her fair hair in a tight, hard little knob, held in place by a tight elastic band on her capacious sun-hat instead of hat pins. She does not look like a traditional old maid and wears oddities of attire.

_Sources: [v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019), [v4 c11 P17](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0017)_

## Personality

Outspoken, opinionated, and pragmatic, Miss Cornelia is famous for abusing and criticizing men at every opportunity, though she maintains a kind heart and is always ready to render tender help in times of trouble. She possesses a bitter, sharp tongue and holds strong prejudices, especially against Methodists and men in general, yet she is deeply loyal and affectionate toward her close friends. Despite her cynical humor regarding obituaries and suitors, she admits to feeling like a lonely soul.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P38](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0038), [v4 c6 P40](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0040), [v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019), [v4 c8 P59](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0059), [v4 c8 P76](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0076), [v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005), [v4 c28 P5](../source/v04-c28.md#nw-v04-c28-p0005)_

## History

Cornelia Bryant grew up as an only child for eight years before praying for a brother, whom she ultimately doted upon and raised after her mother passed away. Following her brother's early death in his twenties and the rejection of various suitors in her youth, she settled into life as an outspoken old maid in Four Winds. She developed strong friendships with her neighbor Leslie Moore, Captain Jim, and Doctor Dave. Upon the arrival of Gilbert and Anne Blythe, Cornelia immediately struck up a warm friendship with Anne and spent much of her time visiting their home, sewing elaborate clothes for neglected neighborhood babies, and entertaining them with sharp commentary. During Anne's illness and recovery, Cornelia spent a great deal of her time cooking delicacies for her. Later, to the surprise of neighbors who knew her anti-male rhetoric, she accepted a marriage proposal from her long-time acquaintance Marshall Elliott.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P40](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0040), [v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019), [v4 c8 P27](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0027), [v4 c8 P59](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0059), [v4 c8 P75](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0075), [v4 c8 P76](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0076), [v4 c10 P38](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0038), [v4 c18 P15](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0015), [v4 c19 P41](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0041), [v4 c34 P26](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0026), [v4 c34 P28](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0028), [v4 c37 P8](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0008), [v4 c38 P37](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0037)_

## Background by volume

- named after her mother Anne  <sub>[v4 c8 P79](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0079)</sub>
- daughter of Stephen Irving  <sub>[v4 c15 P41](../source/v04-c15.md#nw-v04-c15-p0041)</sub>
- was an only child for eight years before her younger brother was born  <sub>[v4 c34 P26](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0026)</sub>
- raised her younger brother after their mother died when he was under three  <sub>[v4 c34 P28](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0028)</sub>
- her younger brother died in his twenties  <sub>[v4 c28 P7](../source/v04-c28.md#nw-v04-c28-p0007), [v4 c34 P28](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0028)</sub>
- could have had her pick of suitors when young  <sub>[v4 c6 P40](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0040)</sub>
- courted long ago by Amos Grant  <sub>[v4 c37 P16](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0016)</sub>
- won first prize for lemon pies at the Charlottetown Exhibition ten years prior  <sub>[v4 c10 P35](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0035)</sub>

> I’m a kind of lonely soul, Mrs. Blythe.  <sub>[v4 c8 P76](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0076)</sub>

> Yes, I’m the best sewer in these parts. I ought to be!  <sub>[v4 c8 P27](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0027)</sub>

> The Lord has given and the Lord has taken away, dearie. Blessed be the name of the Lord.  <sub>[v4 c19 P22](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0022)</sub>

> I’m not going to marry the best man in the world. Marshall Elliott is a long way from being the best.  <sub>[v4 c37 P8](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0008)</sub>
